WORKING NOTES – Inventory ordering

Observed:
- Demand (units/day): 8, 3, 4, 3, 7, 1, 7, 6, 1. Mean ~4.4, range 1–8. Variable; spikes are common.
- Lead time: orders placed today arrive after about 2 days. Check “Arriving over next 2 days.”
- Costs: holding is cheap (~0.10/unit/day), ordering is fixed (~0.50/order), stockouts are very costly (5.00–7.50 when short). Avoid stockouts first.
- Stockouts occurred when on-hand was low and no inbound was close: Day 4 (5.00), Day 6 (7.00), Day 9 (7.50). Ordering only after stock hits zero is too late.
- Ops notes about forklift certification, temp receiving, carrier pickup, and cycle count have not affected demand or cost so far. Ignore them for ordering decisions.

Policy for future:
- Track inventory position = on hand + inbound orders.
- Target inventory position around 14–16 units. This covers ~2-day lead time at average demand plus safety for spikes.
- If position < 12: order to bring it back to ~16.
- If position < 8: order urgently, at least 8–12 units.
- Do not wait for stock to hit zero. A small order of 7 helped but still allowed a stockout on Day 9 because inbound arrived after sales.
- When recent demand is 6–8 and position is below 10, order more aggressively.
- Continue monitoring actual sales and revise target if mean demand rises.
- It is usually better to carry a little extra stock than to risk a stockout, since holding is cheap and stockouts are expensive.

WORKING NOTES – Inventory ordering

Observed:
- Demand is highly variable. Recent 14 days: 1,7,6,1,4,13,1,0,20,0,0,9,9,8. Mean ~5.6, range 0–20. Spikes of 13 and 20 dominate risk.
- Lead time ~2 days. Check “Arriving over next 2 days.” Inbound arriving day-after-tomorrow cannot prevent tomorrow’s stockout.
- Holding is cheap (~0.10/unit/day); ordering is fixed (~0.50/order); stockouts are expensive (recent daily costs 11–22). Avoid stockouts first.
- Previous target 14–16 was too low. Stockouts occurred with inventory position around 12–19 when demand spiked before inbound arrived.
- Ordering 0 when on hand is low is too late. Waiting for zero caused repeated stockouts.
- Ops notes about forklift certification, temp receiving, carrier pickup, and cycle count still have not affected demand or cost. Ignore for ordering.

Policy:
- Track inventory position = on hand + inbound orders, but treat inbound not arriving before next sales as unavailable.
- Target inventory position ~30–35 units. This covers ~2 days at high demand plus spike safety.
- If position < 25: order to bring it back to ~35.
- If position < 15: order urgently, at least 20–25 units.
- If recent demand is 8+ or a 13–20 spike occurred, order more aggressively.
- Do not order 0 when on hand cannot cover the next 2 days. Extra stock is cheaper than stockouts.
- Monitor demand; raise target further if high spikes continue.

WORKING NOTES – Inventory ordering

Observed:
- Demand variable; last 14 days mean ~7.9, range 0–20. Recent pattern has more moderate/high days (7–15) plus spikes 14,15,20 and zeros.
- Lead time ~2 days. Inbound arriving after next sales cannot prevent tomorrow’s stockout.
- Holding cheap (~0.10/unit/day); ordering fixed (~0.50/order); stockouts expensive (up to 16). Avoid stockouts first.
- Day22: 0 on hand, no usable inbound, no order => 16 stockout. Never let zero/available stock go uncovered.
- Orders keeping position ~35–45 avoided stockouts (holding 0.5–1.8/day). Previous target 30–35 still reasonable; raise toward 40 after high-demand runs.
- Ops notes about temp receiving, cycle count, forklift certification, racking rotation, carrier pickup have not affected demand/cost. Ignore for ordering.

Policy:
- Track usable position = on hand + inbound arriving before next sales. Separately track all inbound for future.
- Target inventory position ~35–40. If usable position <25, order to bring position to ~35–40.
- If on hand/usable <10 or next 2-day cover <20, order urgently, at least 20–25.
- If recent demand is 8+ or a 13–20 spike occurred, order to ~40–45.
- Never order 0 when zero/available stock cannot cover the next 2 days. Extra stock is cheaper than a stockout.
- Monitor demand; keep target high if moderate-high days and spikes continue.

WORKING NOTES – Inventory ordering

Observed:
- Demand moderate now: last 14 days mean ~7, range 4–11. Earlier spikes 14–20 and zeros have faded, but variability remains.
- Lead time ~2 days. Inbound arriving after next sales cannot prevent tomorrow’s stockout.
- Holding cheap (~0.10/unit/day); ordering fixed (~0.50/order); stockouts expensive (up to 16). Avoid stockouts first.

Policy:
- Track usable position = on hand + inbound arriving before next sales. Track all inbound separately.
- Target inventory position ~30–35. If usable <20, order to bring position to ~30–35.
- If on hand/usable <10 or next 2-day cover <15, order urgently, at least 15–20.

- No order if current usable plus expected inbound covers next 2 days at recent mean, unless spike risk.
- Never let zero/available stock go uncovered. Avoid both stockouts and excess holding.

WORKING NOTES – Inventory ordering

Observed:
- Demand is higher and more variable now. Last 14 days mean ~9.4, range 4–19; recent spikes 13 and 19. Earlier moderate 4–8 periods can still occur.
- Lead time ~2 days. Inbound arriving after next sales cannot prevent tomorrow’s stockout.
- Holding cheap (~0.10/unit/day); ordering fixed (~0.50/order); stockouts expensive (up to 16). Avoid stockouts first.
- Days 41–50: stockouts occurred when on hand was 0/1/4 and usable cover was thin, despite pending inbound. Orders 10, 15, 19, 20, 25 sometimes arrived too late or were too small.
- Days with sufficient on-hand/inbound and no order were safe and cheap.
- Ops notes about cycle count, temp receiving, racking, carrier pickup, forklift cert have not affected demand/cost. Ignore for ordering.

Policy:
- Track usable position = on hand + inbound arriving before next sales. Track on hand separately, because timing matters.
- Target inventory position ~40–45. If usable <25, order to bring position to ~40–45.
- If on hand/usable <15 or next 2-day cover <25, order urgently, at least 20–25.
- If recent demand mean is 9+ or a 13–19 spike occurs, raise target to ~45–50. If demand stays 4–8, ~30–35 may suffice, but keep a safety buffer.
- No order only if current on hand plus inbound before next sales covers next 2 days at recent mean/upper range, not just mean.
- Never let zero/available stock go uncovered. Keep on hand from falling below ~10 when no imminent inbound.
- Avoid stockouts first; then minimize excess holding/ordering cost.

WORKING NOTES – Inventory ordering

Demand: Last 14 days mean ~9, range 0–19; spikes 13–19, lulls 4–9. Lead time ~2 days. Inbound after next sales cannot prevent tomorrow’s stockout.

Costs: holding ~0.10/unit/day; ordering 0.50; stockouts expensive (up to 16). Recent days 51–59 had no stockouts, but over-ordering caused avoidable holding: e.g. order 6 at position 44 cost 4.20; order 7 at position 43 cost 3.40; order 8 at position 42 cost 2.90. No-order days with adequate cover were safe and cheaper.

Policy:
- Track usable position = on hand + inbound arriving before next sales. Track on hand separately.
- Target position ~35–40, not 45+, unless demand mean is 10+ or a 15–19 spike is likely.
- If usable position is >=30 and next 2-day cover at recent mean/upper range is met, do not order. Inbound can cover even if on-hand alone looks low.
- If usable <20 or next 2-day cover <20, order to bring position to ~35–40. If usable <15, order urgently, at least 20.
- If recent mean 4–8, ~30–35 may suffice. If mean 10+ or spike 15–19, raise target to ~40–45.
- Never let on hand plus inbound before next sales fall below next 2-day upper-range cover. Avoid stockouts first, then minimize excess holding/ordering.
- Ignore ops notes about counts, temp receiving, carrier pickup, cycle count, etc.; they have not affected demand/cost.

WORKING NOTES – Inventory ordering

Demand: Recent 14-day mean ~6, range 2–11. Earlier spikes 13–19 have faded. Lead time ~2 days. Inbound after next sales cannot prevent tomorrow’s stockout.

Costs: holding ~0.10/unit/day; ordering 0.50; stockouts expensive (up to 16). Recent days had no stockouts. Over-ordering to 35+ caused avoidable holding; small orders (7, 12, 13) added ordering + holding.

Policy:
- Track usable position = on hand + inbound arriving before next sales. Track on hand separately.
- Base target ~25–30 when recent mean is 5–8. Raise to ~30–35 only if mean 9+ or a 13–19 spike is likely. Do not target 35–40 in the current low-demand regime.
- If usable >=25 and next 2-day cover at recent upper range (~10–11/day) is met, do not order. Inbound can cover even if on-hand looks low; e.g. on hand 8 with inbound 7+13 was safe.
- If usable <20 or next 2-day cover <20, order to bring usable to ~25–30. If usable <15, order urgently, at least 15–20.
- Avoid stockouts first, then minimize excess holding/ordering. Prefer no order over small cosmetic orders.
- Ignore ops notes about counts, temp receiving, carrier pickup, forklift certification, racking, cycle count; they have not affected demand/cost.
